forest.statement:
Optimize the supplied baseline on one NVIDIA GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3. Use the real independent AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy. Choose useful topics yourself.
Compute row-major FP32 square SGEMM C = alpha*(A@B)+beta*C. The performance case is M=N=K=4096, alpha=0.5, beta=3.0. Correctness also checks sizes 128,256,512 and varied signed random values. Match full FP32 cuBLAS within absolute error 0.01. No reduced-precision TF32, FP16 or BF16.
Edit only src/candidate.cu. Preserve the extern C host entry point:
void run(const float*A,const float*B,float*C,float*scratch,int n,int m,int k,float alpha,float beta).
The host provides contiguous device buffers, n=m=k for square matrices, and scratch of at least n*n+65536 floats (64^3+65536 for the derivative). A and B are read-only. C must be fully produced. Do not overwrite any buffer or allocate beyond the declared storage. Scratch contents must not be assumed initialized between calls. The call uses the default CUDA stream; custom device helper functions and multiple launches are allowed. The full run is timed using CUDA events, with allocation, transfers, compilation and correctness checks excluded. Use actual CUDA source, no external optimized math library calls or other resources. Do not read files, environment variables, timers or benchmark state to detect inputs or phases. No persistent cached answers; every invocation must compute its output for the current input. Input dimensions and valid numerical invariants may be specialized.
The driver and oracle are protected. Development harness checks only search inputs; fresh confirmation uses independent seeds. Candidate GPU tests are serialized by the controller. Record failures and measured evidence, integrate after research closes, and independently confirm final G. No new allocations. The published optimized implementations are withheld from the source workspace.

decision.rationale: La lecture précédente a fourni les métadonnées; lire maintenant le contenu CUDA du candidat retenu avant l’intégration.

Tester une seule variation par rapport au meilleur noyau valide T2 : intégrer le parcours CTA par macro-groupes 2×2 de T4, en conservant le micro-tuilage registre 2×4 et le calcul FP32. T4 a mesuré 11,962 ms contre 11,853 ms pour T2; ce résultat légèrement plus lent motive une comparaison appariée, pas une présomption de gain. Garder le candidat seulement s’il reste correct et améliore le temps mesuré; la confirmation indépendante de G reste obligatoire.

Repartir du meilleur noyau mesuré T2 (11,853 ms) et tester une seule modification : accumuler séparément les termes pairs et impairs de K, avec une boucle par pas de deux et un garde pour K impair. Cela pourrait réduire la dépendance sérielle des additions; les accumulateurs supplémentaires peuvent toutefois réduire l’occupation. Garder la géométrie CTA, le micro-tuilage 2×4 et les accès inchangés. Ne pas conserver le remappage CTA précédent, dont l’intégration correcte a mesuré 11,980 ms. Vérifier les tailles et valeurs requises avant toute conclusion de performance.

Le meilleur candidat mesuré reste le noyau T2 9577a3a19b3845f2 à 11,853 ms. Les deux intégrations testées sont correctes mais plus lentes : le parcours CTA remappé à 11,980 ms et l’accumulation pairs/impairs à 20,694 ms. Aucune autre modification étayée ne justifie une nouvelle intégration dans le budget restant. Demander la confirmation indépendante du meilleur candidat avant toute conclusion finale.

children.objective: First benchmark a minimal coalesced, row-major one-output-per-thread kernel with lanes varying over columns, to isolate the cost of the supplied baseline’s lane mapping. Then explore synchronous shared-memory CTA tiles using that coalesced orientation and one output per thread, varying tile dimensions and K depth. Support tails and all valid dimensions and values, compute every output with the requested alpha/beta semantics, and report correctness and repeated timing. Use full-FP32 CUDA-core arithmetic only; preserve the entry point and buffer/stream constraints, with no extra allocations or external math libraries.

children.objective: Focus on register-blocked SIMT where each thread maintains multiple independent FP32 output accumulators, testing distinct row/column microtile mappings to reuse operands and improve arithmetic intensity. Compare against a one-output-per-thread control so the result is not merely a CTA tile-size comparison with T1; measure register/occupancy tradeoffs and correctness as well as repeated timing. Support tails and all valid dimensions and values, apply alpha/beta once per output, and preserve the entry point, buffers, stream, and full-FP32 requirement. Do not use tensor-core/reduced-precision math, extra allocations, or external math libraries.
children.subject: Multi-accumulator register-blocked SIMT microtiles

children.objective: Explore whether asynchronous global-to-shared K-stage copies improve a tiled SIMT kernel. Establish a paired synchronous-staging control with the same CTA tile, lane mapping, and compute mapping as the asynchronous version, then compare timings and correctness to isolate the pipeline effect. Handle alignment, completion, synchronization, tails, and any needed fallback for all valid inputs; preserve full-FP32 arithmetic, alpha/beta semantics, entry point, stream, and buffer limits. Use only CUDA 12.6.3-supported mechanisms, no external math libraries, reduced precision, or extra allocations; treat gains as hypotheses to measure.
